$comment: The four kinds of id the protocol names, each a schema under components/schemas with the rule it is held to as its `pattern`. `properties` are the property names that always carry that kind, wherever they appear in the spec; `accepts` and `refuses` are strings the rule takes and does not, each with why. `others` are properties named like an id that carry something else. scripts/spec/check-identifiers.mjs holds the spec to this file: every property so named refers to its kind, every case agrees with its kind's pattern, and a property whose name ends in `Id` or `Ids` that is in neither list fails. Each SDK's checked constructors run the same cases.

the scope events about the knowledge base itself are logged under
how an id is made is not part of the rule

refuses.why: an id names something
an id is one name in a file system, and this one names the directory above

no `.` at all: a store appends an extension to an id to name a file
an id is one segment of a path
on any file system
a URI is not an id: the id is its last segment
no whitespace

nothing that needs encoding, and nothing already encoded
nothing a URL reads as its own
nothing a URL reads as its own
ASCII only: one spelling, on every file system
129 characters: a file's name has a limit, and an id is well inside it
